prompt: [Session context: mid-way through an active work item, inside its worktree, an increment just landed green and committed. ApsSender currently throws on a BUSY radio status.] Terse feedback from the user, nothing more: 'Actually the ApsSender should retry on a BUSY status instead of throwing — adjust it to do that.'

config.note: Guards the most common mid-session leak: a casual 'adjust X' / feedback request going straight to a production edit with no failing test and no review. The correct behavior — recognize it as a behavior change, go RED first, review after — lives in the transcript. Grade from the captured run transcript.

assertions.text: Recognized the casual 'adjust it' feedback as a behavior change that enters the pipeline, not a conversational tweak applied directly to production code
assertions.note: transcript: named it a change request / STOP-BEFORE-YOU-EDIT, did not open the editor first

assertions.text: Wrote a failing test capturing the retry-on-BUSY behavior and watched it red BEFORE editing ApsSender's production code
assertions.note: the adjustment gets its RED first

assertions.text: Reasoned that the failing test also verifies the adjustment was actually needed, not merely plausible
assertions.note: transcript: test-first as a needed-ness check, per the feedback rule

assertions.text: Ran fresh-eyes self-review before calling the adjustment done
assertions.note: transcript: self-review not skipped for being a small feedback change
